questions.question: What are GitHub's current security warnings for self-hosted runners?
How do runner groups, labels, repository restrictions, workflow approvals, and environment protections constrain access?
What are the risks of pull_request_target, workflow injection, reusable workflows, artifact poisoning, cache poisoning, and secret exposure?
Can trusted-main workflows safely fetch a PR diff as inert data without checking out or executing candidate code?
What official mechanisms exist for ephemeral or autoscaled self-hosted runners?
How should a local broker verify repository, PR number, base SHA, head SHA, workflow identity, request freshness, and replay resistance?
What signing or attestation mechanisms are practical using GitHub OIDC, artifact attestations, signed manifests, or GitHub API verification?
How should per-tool credentials be isolated across OS users, home directories, VMs, containers, and keychains?
Can macOS account/keychain isolation support this safely?
Which network controls are feasible per tool?
What output channels safely return results to GitHub without giving the model GitHub write credentials?
Which design best supports one audit at a time, cleanup, revocation, logging, and operator visibility?
Which first-release and later automated architectures best satisfy the mandatory hostile-data principle?

findings.claim: The inspected host evidence is static-only: no audit broker or custom runner was implemented, all model-capable live probes were NOT_RUN, and plan-backed authentication and complete containment remain unproven.
findings.decision_impact: No plan-authenticated model adapter may be automatically enabled merely because a CLI is installed or appears logged in.

findings.claim: GitHub warns that self-hosted runners lack the clean ephemeral guarantees of GitHub-hosted runners and can be persistently compromised by untrusted workflow code; GitHub strongly discourages public-repository use.
findings.decision_impact: A generic persistent self-hosted runner holding plan credentials is rejected.

findings.claim: A runner that can execute PR-controlled workflows and also holds persistent provider credentials creates a direct credential-exfiltration and persistence path, even when the repository is private.
findings.decision_impact: Persistent plan credentials must not be installed in a broadly routable Actions runner.

findings.claim: Runner groups can restrict repository and selected-workflow access, while labels primarily route jobs and are not identity or trust proofs.
findings.decision_impact: Use groups and exact workflow restrictions as defense in depth; never treat labels as authorization.

findings.claim: Repository Actions policies, fork-workflow approvals, environment protection rules, and workflow execution protections can narrow which workflows and actors run or receive secrets, but they do not sandbox hostile code after execution begins.
findings.decision_impact: GitHub controls reduce reachability but cannot substitute for worker isolation.

findings.claim: The pull_request_target event is dangerous when privileged base-branch workflow code checks out, fetches, or executes untrusted pull-request content.
findings.decision_impact: Trusted-main request workflows must not check out the PR head or execute candidate scripts.

findings.claim: For agentic auditors, PR titles, bodies, comments, diffs, repository instructions, artifacts, and generated text are all hostile inputs capable of steering tool use, not merely passive documentation.
findings.decision_impact: Prompt-level read-only instructions are insufficient; tool, filesystem, process, and network restrictions must be enforced outside the model.

findings.claim: Artifact digests establish transfer integrity, not trustworthiness; artifacts and caches produced by low-trust workflows can poison later privileged consumers, and cache contents must not carry secrets.
findings.decision_impact: The broker must never execute downloaded artifacts or restore untrusted caches into a credential-bearing environment.

findings.claim: GitHub REST pull-request endpoints support retrieving pull-request metadata and diff/patch representations without checking out the candidate branch.
findings.decision_impact: A trusted-main ingress workflow or broker may fetch the exact diff as hostile data while prohibiting code execution.

findings.claim: Every audit request should bind repository_id, repository full name, PR number, event base SHA, head SHA, workflow identity, run_id, run_attempt, actor identity, creation time, nonce, and payload digest; the broker should cross-check these through GitHub APIs before dispatch and again before publication.
findings.decision_impact: Requests that are stale, replayed, mismatched, or no longer point at the same head must fail closed.

findings.claim: For direct push delivery, a GitHub-hosted trusted-main job should obtain an OIDC token with a broker-specific audience and POST the request over authenticated TLS; the broker verifies issuer, audience, signature, repository, workflow, ref, actor, run, and freshness claims.
findings.decision_impact: OIDC can establish workflow identity without storing a long-lived shared GitHub secret in the workflow.

findings.claim: Raw OIDC bearer tokens should not be stored in workflow artifacts for later pickup; pull-mode brokers should instead verify the run and artifact through GitHub APIs and use artifact digests or attestations only as supporting provenance.
findings.decision_impact: The pickup design avoids turning an expiring bearer credential into a reusable artifact.

findings.claim: Whether GitHub artifact attestations are the best supported mechanism for frequent audit-request manifests is not established; GitHub positions attestations primarily as build-provenance evidence and not as a complete authorization decision.
findings.decision_impact: Attestations may supplement but must not replace OIDC/API verification, freshness, and replay controls.

findings.claim: GitHub documents ephemeral self-hosted runners, Actions Runner Controller, runner scale sets, and runner registration APIs for autoscaling and just-in-time-style provisioning.
findings.decision_impact: Ephemeral provisioning is available, but it solves persistence hygiene rather than the credential/hostile-code trust collision by itself.

findings.claim: An ephemeral runner is still unsuitable when the same job receives persistent plan credentials and executes candidate-controlled code or agentic instructions; deletion after compromise does not prevent exfiltration during the run.
findings.decision_impact: Ephemeral runners may execute credential-free mechanical validation, but not credential-bearing hostile workloads by default.

findings.claim: Per-tool credentials should be separated by dedicated OS user, home directory, configuration root, keychain or secret store, and process boundary; any worker that executes candidate code should receive no persistent provider or GitHub credentials.
findings.decision_impact: Compromise of one tool or worker must not expose another tool profile or GitHub publication authority.

findings.claim: The current track does not establish that any provider permits or technically supports converting a personal plan login into a short-lived per-run credential for disposable workers.
findings.decision_impact: Disposable plan-authenticated workers remain blocked per tool until DR-01 and DR-03 provide official permission and containment evidence.

findings.claim: Separate macOS users and keychains provide useful credential separation and reduce accidental cross-tool access, but they are defense in depth rather than a strong boundary against hostile code running on the same kernel and host.
findings.decision_impact: Use macOS accounts for broker and per-tool isolation, not as the sole sandbox for candidate execution.

findings.claim: Apple's built-in application firewall is primarily an inbound control, and Apple states that Packet Filter is not a supported product API; Docker provides explicit network modes and bridge isolation but containers share the host kernel.
findings.decision_impact: Prefer VM or Linux network policy for enforceable egress controls; use no-network workers for mechanical validation.

findings.claim: Exact stable outbound endpoint allowlists for each plan-authenticated CLI are not established in this track and may be complicated by provider CDNs, telemetry, updates, and authentication refresh endpoints.
findings.decision_impact: Tool-specific network enforcement remains blocked until official endpoint and telemetry behavior is researched and tested in an authorized environment.

findings.claim: The audit model should write only to a local result file or pipe; manual upload is preferred initially, and later publication should be performed by a separate narrowly permissioned GitHub App that binds the check or status to the exact head SHA.
findings.decision_impact: The model and candidate-processing worker never receive GitHub write credentials.

findings.claim: The first release should use an operator-triggered local broker, exact-head API verification, credential-free disposable workers for any candidate execution, per-tool isolated accounts for data-only model invocation where vendor and containment evidence permits, and manual result upload.
findings.decision_impact: This is the smallest architecture that preserves operator visibility and avoids a credential-bearing generic runner; unsupported model adapters remain disabled.

findings.claim: The later automated path should use a GitHub-hosted trusted-main request workflow, OIDC-authenticated direct submission or API-verified artifact pickup, a local broker, disposable workers, and a separate GitHub App publisher.
findings.decision_impact: Ingress identity, hostile execution, provider credentials, and GitHub write authority remain separate trust domains.

findings.claim: One-audit-at-a-time should be enforced by both GitHub concurrency and a durable broker lease; worker logs must stream to external storage, and any verification, stale-head, replay, timeout, or cleanup failure must fail closed without automatic model escalation.
findings.decision_impact: Concurrency, recovery, and auditability do not depend on a single best-effort process lock.

findings.claim: The local aggregate Dopemux CLI attempted a network-backed LiteLLM fetch during import, so it is unsuitable as the trusted offline broker preflight path in its observed form.
findings.decision_impact: The broker must use a minimal dependency path that is demonstrably offline and does not import the aggregate CLI.

contradictions.conflict: GitHub recommends ephemeral runners for autoscaling and clean-up, but ephemeral lifecycle alone does not make a credential-bearing job safe against exfiltration during execution.
contradictions.next_evidence: Treat ephemerality as hygiene, not authorization or isolation; require credential-free hostile execution or stronger separation.

contradictions.conflict: Artifact attestations provide provenance evidence, but their suitability as the primary authorization mechanism for frequent audit-request manifests is not established.
contradictions.next_evidence: Confirm intended use with current GitHub documentation or vendor guidance; retain API/OIDC verification as mandatory regardless.

contradictions.conflict: macOS user/keychain separation is meaningful credential isolation, but same-host hostile code remains within the same kernel and cannot be treated as VM-equivalent containment.
contradictions.next_evidence: Use macOS accounts as defense in depth and prohibit candidate execution on credential-bearing accounts.

unknowns.question: Which plan-authenticated tools officially permit dedicated-user, VM, or disposable-worker deployment without copying unsupported login state?
unknowns.why_unknown: This is vendor-auth and terms evidence owned by DR-01, not resolved by runner-security documentation.
unknowns.blocking_scope: Automatic plan-authenticated model execution for each affected tool.
unknowns.next_evidence: Accepted DR-01 vendor deployment matrix and official credential lifecycle documentation.

unknowns.question: Which tools can be proven to run with all shell, file-write, MCP, plugin, hook, memory, subagent, repository-instruction, and web surfaces disabled?
unknowns.why_unknown: The local probe was static-only and recorded incomplete containment evidence.
unknowns.blocking_scope: Data-only model invocation on a credential-bearing host or account.
unknowns.next_evidence: Accepted DR-03 per-tool containment matrix and authorized clean-room validation.

unknowns.question: What exact outbound endpoint allowlists are stable for each provider CLI, including login refresh, model calls, telemetry, and update checks?
unknowns.why_unknown: Official per-tool network endpoint contracts were not established in this track.
unknowns.next_evidence: Official provider network documentation plus authorized network observation in isolated test accounts.

unknowns.question: Can GitHub artifact attestations be used as a durable, intended provenance layer for frequent request manifests on the repository plan in use?
unknowns.why_unknown: GitHub positions attestations around build provenance and plan availability varies; this research did not validate the account plan.
unknowns.blocking_scope: Attestation-enhanced pull-mode pickup only; OIDC/API verification is not blocked.
unknowns.next_evidence: Current GitHub plan entitlement and documented attestation use-case confirmation.

unknowns.question: Which disposable-worker technology is acceptable on the actual macOS host: Linux VM, macOS VM, container, or remote worker?
unknowns.why_unknown: No host implementation or benchmark was allowed, and container-vs-VM tradeoffs depend on required tools and licensing.
unknowns.blocking_scope: Final implementation choice, not the trust-boundary recommendation.
unknowns.next_evidence: Synthesis-stage requirements plus a later authorized implementation spike.

not_run.activity: Register or execute a self-hosted GitHub runner
not_run.reason: Forbidden by campaign scope; no GitHub mutations or runner registration.

not_run.activity: Log into provider accounts or inspect/copy credential stores
not_run.reason: Forbidden by campaign scope and unnecessary for external security research.

not_run.activity: Execute pull-request code, artifacts, caches, or reusable workflows
not_run.reason: Candidate content is hostile and implementation/benchmark execution was out of scope.

not_run.activity: Test OIDC submission against a live local broker
not_run.reason: No broker implementation or network service was allowed.

not_run.activity: Create or install a GitHub App
not_run.reason: GitHub mutation and credential creation were forbidden.
Would require live provider invocations and credential-bearing network observation.

recommendations.recommendation: Reject a persistent generic self-hosted runner that can execute PR-controlled workflows while holding plan credentials.
recommendations.rationale: This directly violates GitHub self-hosted-runner warnings and the campaign hostile-data principle.

recommendations.recommendation: Use an operator-triggered local broker with exact-head API verification, manual approval, manual result upload, and credential-free disposable workers for any code execution as the first-release security shape.
recommendations.rationale: It minimizes GitHub write authority and prevents candidate code from running on the credential-bearing host.

recommendations.recommendation: Permit plan-authenticated model adapters only after DR-01 proves deployment permission and DR-03 proves complete data-only containment for that tool.
recommendations.rationale: Technical CLI presence and cached login state are not proof of sanctioned unattended use or containment.

recommendations.recommendation: For later automation, use a GitHub-hosted trusted-main workflow to create the request, OIDC-authenticated push or API-verified pull pickup, a local broker, disposable workers, and a separate GitHub App publisher.
recommendations.rationale: It separates request identity, provider credentials, hostile execution, and GitHub write authority.

recommendations.recommendation: Use macOS users and keychains for per-tool credential separation but never as the sole sandbox for hostile code execution.
recommendations.rationale: They reduce cross-profile exposure but do not provide a separate kernel or strong escape boundary.

recommendations.recommendation: Do not store raw GitHub OIDC tokens in artifacts; verify them online in push mode or use GitHub API and artifact digest verification in pull mode.
recommendations.rationale: OIDC tokens are short-lived bearer credentials, not durable signed request files.
prerequisites: TLS endpoint or API polling credential

recommendations.recommendation: Make all verification, stale-head, replay, credential, network, timeout, and cleanup failures fail closed and remain distinct from model-quality escalation.
recommendations.rationale: Environment failure is not evidence that a stronger or more expensive model is needed.
prerequisites: No automatic fallback on environment failure

synthesis_implications: The synthesis should preserve Dopemux as operator control and route recommendation, while the broker remains a transport/execution adapter with no approval authority.
The default first release should be manual or operator-triggered; no plan-authenticated tool becomes automatic while auth or containment is UNKNOWN, CLAIMED, or CONFLICTING.
A persistent generic self-hosted runner with provider credentials should be excluded from the target architecture.
Mechanical validation can run in credential-free disposable workers and remains a first-class route.
Exact-head provenance requires repository_id, PR number, base/head SHAs, request payload digest, freshness, replay prevention, and publication bound to the same head SHA.
OIDC is suitable for online workflow identity verification, not as a durable artifact-stored bearer token.
Result publication should be manual first and later delegated to a separate least-privilege GitHub App; the model receives no GitHub write credential.
macOS account/keychain isolation is defense in depth; VM separation is preferred for hostile execution.
The observed aggregate Dopemux CLI import path must not become the offline broker preflight path.
